## Summary

I implemented the AG-UI deprecation surface for the upcoming major version. All eight requirements are satisfied and verified end-to-end.

### Source changes

1. **`pydantic_ai/_warnings.py`** — `PydanticAIDeprecationWarning` now subclasses `DeprecationWarning` (while keeping `UserWarning` in the MRO for back-compat), so `pytest.warns`/`filterwarnings` can match it on the standard category. Docstring updated to reflect the new rationale.

2. **`pydantic_ai/ag_ui.py`** — emits a module-import-time warning: `The \`pydantic_ai.ag_ui\` module is deprecated, use \`pydantic_ai.ui.ag_ui\` instead.` It still exports `handle_ag_ui_request` and `run_ag_ui` (and the rest) for backward compatibility.

3. **`pydantic_ai/agent/abstract.py`** — `Agent.to_ag_ui()` now warns `\`Agent.to_ag_ui()\` is deprecated, …`.

4. **`pydantic_ai/ui/ag_ui/app.py`** — `AGUIApp.__init__` warns `\`AGUIApp\` is deprecated, …` on every instantiation, with or without extra kwargs (before the existing `builtin_tools=` handling).

5. **`pyproject.toml`** — added three `ignore:` `filterwarnings` entries for the new deprecation messages, exactly mirroring the existing pattern used for `instrument`/`AgentSpec.instrument`. This keeps the many existing tests that exercise these legacy APIs (and the re-emit behavior of `pytest.warns`) from failing under the global `filterwarnings=["error"]`, while dedicated tests can still assert the warnings via `pytest.warns` (which resets filters to `always`).

The `pydantic_ai.ui` (`SSE_CONTENT_TYPE`, `OnCompleteFunc`, `StateDeps`) and `pydantic_ai.ui.ag_ui` (`AGUIAdapter`, `AGUIEventStream`) exports were already present and confirmed.

- A script confirms all 8 requirements (subclass check, all exports, and all three deprecation-warning messages).
- Existing suites pass: `tests/test_ag_ui.py` (105 passed, 1 skipped), `tests/test_native_tools_deprecation.py` + `test_to_ag_ui` (76 passed, 1 skipped), plus instrument-deprecation tests in `test_capabilities.py`.

One design note worth flagging: making `PydanticAIDeprecationWarning` a `DeprecationWarning` subclass means it's now subject to Python's default "ignore `DeprecationWarning`" runtime filter, which reverses the original UserWarning-based "visible by default" intent documented in that class.
